profile.name: Sneak-Up Dance
profile.tagline: A traditional Pow Wow dance simulating the tactical search for an enemy.
profile.insight: Dancers in the Sneak-Up Dance synchronize their movements to a four-part structure, alternating between bell-shaking gestures during drum rolls and a tactical advance toward the center during the standard Omaha beat.
profile.profile: The Sneak-Up Dance is a traditional performance within the Pow Wow, characterized by its rhythmic shifts between drum rolls and the standard Omaha beat. Dancers engage in a dramatic sequence of movements, simulating the search for an enemy and a tactical advance toward the center of the arena. This dance requires strict adherence to the drum's changing tempo and concludes with a specific pattern of stops and movements across four musical renditions.
profile.profile_long: The Sneak-Up Dance is a central feature of the Pow Wow, a traditional gathering of dancers and singers. It is a highly structured performance that requires the dancer to interpret the changing rhythms of the drum. The dance is organized into four distinct renditions, each following a specific pattern of musical cues. During the first half of each rendition, the drum plays a series of rolls. During these rolls, the dancer shakes their bells and performs gestures that simulate the act of following or seeking out an enemy. This requires the dancer to maintain a high level of alertness and physical expression to convey the narrative of the dance. In the second half of each rendition, the music shifts to a standard Omaha beat. During this phase, the dancers perform the 'sneak-up' movement, which involves advancing toward the center of the arena. The dancers must stop precisely on the last beat of the song, with both feet firmly on the ground, before walking back to the perimeter of the dance area. The structure of the dance changes during the fourth rendition, which does not end like the first three but instead continues with three or four straight Omaha renditions. A key element of the dancer's performance is the management of their regalia, particularly the roach crest feathers. Dancers are expected to keep their heads moving in time with the drum, either nodding quickly or moving from side to side, to ensure the feathers remain spinning. Maintaining this constant motion is considered a hallmark of a skilled dancer. While the Omaha style is generally described as a freestyle form of dancing, the Sneak-Up Dance demands strict adherence to the drum's changing beat. The competition categories for this dance are divided into men, teen, junior, and little boys, reflecting its importance across different age groups within the community.

sections.origins_and_history: The Sneak-Up Dance is a traditional dance performed within the context of the Pow Wow, a gathering of dancers and singers.
sections.how_it_is_danced: The dance follows a pattern of drum rolls and Omaha beats. During drum rolls, dancers shake bells and perform gestures of seeking an enemy. During Omaha beats, dancers advance toward the center, stopping on the final beat of the song, then returning to the perimeter.
sections.music_and_instruments: The music is provided by the drum and singers, utilizing specific drum rolls and the standard Omaha beat.
sections.costume_and_setting: Dancers wear regalia including bells and roach crest feathers, which must be kept spinning through head movements.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: The dance is performed at Pow Wows as a demonstration of skill and traditional narrative, often in a competitive context.

basic_steps: Shake bells and perform seeking gestures during drum rolls.
Advance toward the center of the arena during Omaha beats.
Stop movement completely on the last beat of the song with both feet on the ground.
Walk back to the perimeter of the arena.
teaching.rhythm: Alternating between drum rolls and the standard Omaha beat.
teaching.formation: Dancers move from the perimeter toward the center of the arena.
teaching.level_notes: The dance is divided into categories for men, teens, juniors, and little boys.

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Drum rolls in the first half of renditions, followed by a standard Omaha beat in the second half.
music_profile.musical_form: Four renditions, with the fourth differing by continuing with straight Omaha renditions.
music_profile.sound_description: The music is defined by the contrast between rapid drum rolls and the steady, driving pulse of the Omaha beat.

movement_profile.posture: Upright, with head movements to keep roach crest feathers spinning.
movement_profile.footwork: Advancing steps toward the center; must stop with both feet on the ground on the final beat.
movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Gestures of seeking or following an enemy during drum rolls.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Dancers move from the perimeter toward the center of the arena.
movement_profile.tempo_feel: Responsive to the changing beat of the drum.

signature_moves.name: The Sneak-Up
signature_moves.description: Advancing toward the center of the arena during the Omaha beat phase.

movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Failing to stop on the last beat of the song; failing to keep the roach crest feathers moving.

episode_brief.logline: Discover the precision and narrative power of the Sneak-Up Dance, a staple of the Pow Wow arena.
beats: Introduction to the Pow Wow arena.
The role of the drum and the singers.
The importance of regalia and the roach crest feathers.
Breaking down the drum roll phase and the seeking gestures.
The tactical advance of the Omaha beat.
The discipline of the final stop.
The structure of the four renditions.

lesson_ladder.goal: Master the head movement for the roach crest.
Coordinate bell shaking with drum rolls.
